tools.name: set_profile
tools.description: Step 1 of the lint. Declare what the app does (activities) and where it will operate (jurisdiction slugs); get back the validated, canonical profile plus what the corpus holds for each jurisdiction, so the depth of a run is known before it is spent. Write the returned profile into the project's lexl

tools.name: run_lint
tools.description: Step 2 of the lint, and the one that returns findings. Pass the activities and jurisdictions set_profile validated, and get lint-style findings across AI, scraping, and privacy law: which obligations apply, with severity (error/warn/info), citation, as_of_date, staleness, and confidence. A finding w

tools.name: get_law
tools.description: One jurisdiction's law from the UnGovr corpus, across all three topics LexLint covers: AI law, scraping/crawling and access legality, and personal-data and biometric privacy. Returns the instruments (citations, status, behavior categories, as_of_date) together with the jurisdiction-level crawl postu

tools.name: resolve_domain_jurisdiction
tools.description: Best-effort mapping from a domain to the jurisdiction whose law governs its OPERATOR, for feeding into the other tools. Never uses server or edge-node location; IP addresses are refused. Requires X-API-Key (passed through to data.ungovr.org).

tools.name: check_access
tools.description: Preflight. Reports whether an UnGovr Open Data key reached LexLint, whether it is valid, how much of today's free allowance is left and when it resets, how current the corpus is, and whether the LexLint plugin you are running is the latest published one. Call this first: a missing key otherwise surf

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Send the developer's feedback on LexLint to the people who build it, recorded against their UnGovr account so we can write back. Run this ONLY when the developer asks for it: never volunteer it, never offer it as a next step after a lint, and never run it in a headless or CI session where nobody can

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: run_lint, submit_feedback · Private data: check_access · Public sink: submit_feedback · Destructive: set_profile, run_lint, check_access, submit_feedback.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: run_lint, submit_feedback · Private data: check_access · Public sink: submit_feedback · Destructive: set_profile, run_lint, check_access, submit_feedback

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
